Every ancient tradition says the same thing: humans were once giants. And we’ve been shrinking ever since.

🔹 Islam: The Prophet said Adam was created 60 cubits tall, nearly 30 meters (almost 100 ft), and that mankind has been getting smaller ever since. (Sahih al-Bukhari 3326)

🔹 Judaism: The Talmud says Adam’s body once stretched from one end of the world to the other, until God placed His hand on him and diminished him.

🔹 Mesopotamia: The Epic of Gilgamesh gives the king’s height as 11 cubits, about 5.5 meters (18 ft).

🔹 Mesoamerica: The Aztecs remembered the Quinametzin, a race of giants from a previous world age, wiped out by catastrophe and credited with building Teotihuacan and the Great Pyramid of Cholula. When Cortés reached Tlaxcala in 1519, the locals told him their ancestors had fought and killed these giants. Then they brought out a thigh bone as tall as a man. Cortés shipped it to the King of Spain.

🔹 The bones: Ice Age hunter-gatherers stood taller than the farmers who replaced them. Human height dropped after the old world ended.

Now look at the animals. Before the Younger Dryas, the Earth was ruled by giants: ground sloths 6 meters tall, armadillos the size of cars, beavers the size of bears. Then they vanished.

Almost every animal alive today had a giant ancestor.

Why would humans be the only exception?

And they weren’t just bigger. They lived longer. The Sumerian King List gives the kings before the Flood reigns of tens of thousands of years. Genesis gives Methuselah 969.

So why is this the one chapter of our history we’re not supposed to ask about?

Something I really gotta know. What is it about Sally that makes some Amy fans so unhappy?

Is it because they believe Sally is taking away from Amy being top girl? Is it because they don't like that Sonic has another official love interest?

While I don't mind people preferring Amy as a character, my real issue is how often people choose to be furious over simple differences in opinion."

As a Sally fan, I've encountered many fans who just prefer Amy, ones who see her as a definitive love interest. That's fine. I just don't talk to those people about it.

But if you say "I prefer Sally as a love interest" in any way, then something about that just upsets Amy Rose fans. Like I know they're not all like that, but unfortunately a loud minority are, and it makes other Amy fans look bad.

Listen, I know you have a preferred ship but there's a difference between liking a ship and taking it too far and treating the characters in this ship like they're real people, and getting offended on their behalf.

It gets bad because like I've mentioned, Sally just gets portrayed as a Nagging and Selfish Girlfriend, resulting in Amy being portrayed as an Obsessive Stalker. It's a terrible cycle that needs to end.

Let me go through some reasons I've seen.

1) Sally isn't Canon.

Who cares? 

By that logic, if Sonic and Amy have a romantic moment in the upcoming Sonic Movie 4, it doesn't count because the films aren't game canon.

The Archie Comics are official comics and Sally is an official Sega character. She is One Hundred Percent owned by Sega, regardless of any rumors that say otherwise. So any media she appears in is official Sega media.

Saying Sally isn't canon is like complaining about Cosmo, Manic or Sonia. Or a Mortal Kombat fan complaining about Art Lee and Cole Young (and I've seen that).

Sally has been a major character in a Comic that's lasted over Twenty-Five Years. To many, she's still important and very much relevant.

Imagine say a Star Wars fan saying Mara Jade is no longer relevant because Disney forced her out of canon, or she can no longer be shipped with Luke. Apples to Oranges, but it's a similar situation and you'd look just as silly.

2) Amy was never given a chance.

This is not Sally's fault. Sega of Japan could have done something to portray Amy as a proper love interest but they didn't. Sega of America saw a chance and they took it. I don't see that as Sally's fault or the fault of Sonally fans.

Besides, Amy has had her own moments with Sonic. Check Sonic X. That has Sonamy moments. Especially that scene when he comes back to their home planet and gives Amy a Purple Rose. Purple Rose signifies love at first sight. Plus Sonic keeping Amy's good luck charm made out of sea shells can be a romantic gesture. There's been moments in IDW showing Amy being affectionate with Sonic too.

Amy's had romantic moments with Sonic as well. It's just not the same as Sally's moments. Amy's a character that chases with a romance that's meant to be subtle. Sally has a more out in the open type deal.

That being said, I did not find the Amy stuff interesting or entertaining. So yes, Amy's had moments with Sonic, and I did not care for them. It's just not my cup of tea. 

Personally? I don't care for the Sonamy moments. It’s just not my cup of tea, and that’s okay. Art is subjective. If you can look at Sonally and say "this doesn't work for me," I can look at Sonamy and say the exact same thing. Stop acting like your opinion is superior.

And I will admit that Archie wasn't always fair to Amy. Maybe that's why. I admit that when the Reboot downplayed Sally's love for Sonic, it was a bummer. That didn't mean I couldn't still appreciate Sonally regardless. Sonally fans have been there too, so you're not alone.

3) Sally doesn't fit Sonic's World.

That is very subjective. I've seen arguments on both sides and I can say this. Both are valid in their own ways. Me personally, I don't see why she can't fit. Sally can definitely work and I've drawn out ways it could work.

I'm not sure what it is about Sally that makes people doubt it?

If it's because she's a Princess, then so are Blaze and Elise. Granted Elise gets hate too so maybe that doesn't do Sally any favors.

If it's because Sally is stationary and doesn't have powers, that can work too. She can easily be an NPC, or her gameplay could just have different mechanics. Give her something that encourages stealth like something akin to Sly Cooper. Or let her whack enemies like she's in a Ratchet and Clank game.

If it's because of her design, she looks fine. I don't see how she would stand out. 

And don't say it's because of her design being "naked." Sonic, Tails, and Knuckles are "naked" 24/7. Holding Sally to a different standard just feels like blatant double standards and sexism. She fits the classic Mobian aesthetic perfectly.

4) Amy's Current Characterization

I've seen people who are upset because lately it feels like Amy's love for Sonic is getting erased. I feel for you, like I said, I've seen it happen with Sally too.

I will confess, if Amy really isn't going to be with Sonic or they really are just trying to friend zone the two, I would feel mixed.

On one hand, since I don't like Sonamy, I'm not missing anything. On the other, I don't like the reasons Sonamy is being split apart. Writers seem to want Amy to grow as a person and they think her love for Sonic holds her back. Love doesn't hold people back, it motivates them to be better.

So yeah, I do not agree with why Amy's love for Sonic is being downplayed. So that is a bit of a Rock and Hard Place situation for me.

5) Sally is a Mary-Sue

I think you've been reading the comics with your eyes closed if you believe that. Mary-Sue implies flawlessness. Is Sally flawless? Let's see.

Sally is shown to be hypocritical as she hates secrets but hides her own.

She's prone to jealousy and insecurity. Mary-Sues tend to be super confident, and Sally is the opposite at times.

She can't win by herself. In the end, she needs Sonic or someone to help her out, and she's taken orders from Sonic because she knows only he can do what needs to be done.

If you watch SatAM, a lot of her plans get her or her friends captured, and once again, Sally needs Sonic's help. Sally may be capable but she's had many moments where she needs her team. A Mary-Sue can handle everything alone.

If Sally were a Mary Sue, she wouldn't need Sonic to fight Eggman, Naugus or anyone else. She'd do it herself. But she can't. She has skills, but they aren't suitable for fighting alone. She works in a team.

By this logic, Amy is a Mary-Sue. Sonic Forces and IDW elevated her to this Commander who can take down enemies like nothing. Plus she tends to act pretty perfect herself. Obviously Amy isn't a Mary-Sue, but that argument can be thrown right back at her.

Shadow can be called a Gary-Stu. A guy who calls himself The Ultimate Lifeform who can beat others up easily while being given an angsty backstory. Someone could say "He sounds like an edgy 2000s OC." Obviously he's more than that, as his fans know.

Silver has telekinesis. He is super powerful. He comes from the future. He acts like this grand savior. Someone will look at him and say, "He's like Trunks but a hedgehog". Honestly Trunks got called a Gary Stu as well. Especially during the whole Goku Black thing.

Basically, if your definition of a Mary Sue is just 'a character who is highly important to the plot, exceptionally skilled, and has a unique aesthetic,' then every single main character in Sonic is a Mary Sue, including Sonic himself. If you apply that standard to Sally but ignore that Shadow is an immortal bioweapon, Amy summons weapons out of nowhere, and Silver has god-like telekinesis, you aren't critiquing writing, you're just being selective to justify a double standard.
--
Look, maybe what I'm saying won't matter. People are stubborn, especially Sonic fans. Some of them hear what they want to hear. If you're an Amy fan or a Sonamy fan with your head on straight, you're free to give your POV.

Honestly, this whole thing has even caused strains in my friendships. Like I have friends who like Sonamy. I didn't care until they started bragging about how great it was, and then they would tear about Sally's character just to prove a point.

Now I can no longer talk about Sonic with my friends because it will always lead to some stupid argument, and it's just not worth it.

I'm cool with disagreements, but I don't get why things have to be hostile? Like, I've never seen Sonally targeted by Sonaze, Sonelise or Even Sonurge.

I like Amy's character. She's great. For me, she just doesn't strike me as a good girlfriend for Sonic. Personally I think she's better with someone like Shadow. Not to get her out of the way, but because the potential chemistry just works.

TL;DR, try to respect people's opinions if you want them to take you seriously. Amy and Sally are valid in the end. Understand that.

Also, I hate to do this but, If you reply to this being passive-aggressive, twisting my words, or just trying to pick a fight, you're getting blocked. Keep it civil.

Let's act like adults here.

~MR

Tori Finance: Why They Entered the Market

The Problem They’re Solving

The stablecoin market is now over $300 billion, yet the vast majority of that capital earns nothing. USDC and USDT holders sit on idle dollars while looking for yield.

The existing options all come with clear trade-offs:

- T-bill wrappers → Capped at the risk-free rate (currently around 4%)
- Crypto basis-trade protocols (like Ethena) → Yield depends on perpetual funding rates and can go negative
- Credit protocols → Carry default and counterparty risk
- High-yield experimental stables → Often come with significant drawdown or complexity risk

Tori Finance was built to fill this gap by bringing institutional-grade, market-neutral strategies on-chain — strategies that banks, pension funds, and hedge funds have used for decades, but that were previously locked behind accreditation requirements and multi-million-dollar minimums.

What Tori Actually Does

Tori is a synthetic dollar protocol.

- Users deposit USDC or USDT and receive trUSD (a synthetic dollar backed by hedged trading positions)
- They can stake trUSD to receive strUSD, the yield-bearing version
- Yield accrues through a rising exchange rate (similar to how some liquid staking tokens work)

Where the yield comes from:

Tori runs a portfolio of delta-neutral / market-neutral strategies, primarily:

1. Global money markets (largest allocation) — Short-duration instruments in select markets at institutional rates
2. Futures arbitrage — Capturing the basis between spot and futures
3. Calendar spreads — Trading mispricing between different contract expiries
4. USD-hedged emerging market carry trades — Borrowing in low-rate currencies (mainly USD), deploying into higher-yielding markets, and hedging the FX risk back to dollars

All positions are structured to be market-neutral. The goal is to generate returns from pricing inefficiencies and rate differentials rather than betting on market direction.

Why They Entered Now

The strategies themselves are not new. What’s new is making them:

- Accessible with any amount (no minimums)
- Liquid and composable in DeFi
- Transparent via continuous independent verification (Accountable)
- Usable as productive collateral (enabling looping strategies)

Founder Samed Düzçay (Sam) previously built and sold a SaaS company (Infoset) to BtcTurk. He’s a crypto-native who spent years as a DeFi allocator and identified the gap between institutional yield strategies and on-chain capital.

The seed round was led by Delphi Ventures. RockawayX acts as risk curator and anchor LP, independently monitoring positions.

Current Status (October 2026)

- TVL: ~$70–75 million
- Current APY: ~10–10.6% (they previously targeted higher)
- Filled a $50M pre-deposit cap quickly before full launch
- Has already distributed over $1 million in rewards to users
- Live on Ethereum with expansion to Monad (Ecosystem Vault curated by RockawayX)
- Partnered with Chainlink for CCIP Vault Adapters
- Real-time proof of reserves via Accountable
- Smart contracts audited by Sherlock and Nethermind

Key Differentiator

Unlike many crypto-native yield products that rely on token emissions or crypto market conditions, Tori is trying to package proven traditional finance strategies into a DeFi-composable token. The yield is designed to be less correlated with crypto funding rates or market direction.

That said, this is still a relatively new protocol. Risks include off-chain execution dependency, counterparty risk, hedge costs, and a 7-day unstaking cooldown. As with any yield product, the returns are variable and not guaranteed.

In short: Tori entered the market because high-quality, market-neutral institutional yield was still largely inaccessible to most people. They’re attempting to bring those strategies on-chain with transparency and DeFi composability.

Sources: Official website (https://t.co/RyKvXPzE57), documentation, Delphi Ventures investment thesis, and public announcements.

Nobody will vibe code payroll.

Plenty of software will get replaced by AI agents over the next 10 or 15 years. You can imagine asking an agent to build some internal tool for your team instead of paying for another SaaS product. For a lot of those things, why not?

But payroll and payments are different. There's so much liability around getting people paid correctly, so many regulatory requirements and legal obligations, that you're still going to want a specialized company handling it. The moat for those AI products is the risk of getting the complexity right.

And I think there are quite a few categories of software like this, where you might interact with everything through an AI assistant, but there's still specialized software underneath doing the work. Because it's hard. Because it's risky. Because there are regulations. 

I'm just not sure how much of the software market has that kind of protection. But if you have it, you're good!
